requirements.title: Landing-Page Hero
requirements.definition: The landing-page hero must present the project, ebook offer, referral incentive, mint call to action, and associated visual hierarchy.
requirements.boundary_note: Hero copy and layout can change independently of the FAQ, About pages, and book-cover sizing.

requirements.title: Landing-Page Book Cover
requirements.definition: The ebook cover must be included on the landing page at an aesthetically appropriate size without cropping or obscuring other controls.
requirements.boundary_note: Cover visibility and sizing repeatedly changed independently of the surrounding hero copy.

requirements.title: Project FAQ Content
requirements.definition: The site must provide accurate explanatory FAQ content covering minting, referrals, prizes, wallets, fiat access, fees, secondary sales, and support.
requirements.boundary_note: This Requirement owns published explanatory content, not the underlying business mechanisms described by that content.

requirements.title: NFT Ebook Mint Offer
requirements.definition: The product must sell the ebook as an unlimited-mint NFT on Base at a USD-denominated price of $15.
requirements.boundary_note: The offer defines the asset, network, supply model, and base price; payment rails and revenue distribution are separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Wallet Mint Payment Methods
requirements.definition: Wallet users must be able to select and complete supported USDC or ETH mint payments, with clear currency presentation and controlled conversion/refund behavior.
requirements.boundary_note: USDC approval, ETH conversion, currency selection, and excess-refund policy are attributes of one wallet-payment mechanism.

requirements.title: Fiat On-Ramp
requirements.definition: Non-crypto buyers must eventually be able to purchase through a card-based fiat on-ramp, with the provider and launch timing selected by the client.
requirements.boundary_note: Provider selection and temporary launch deferral are lifecycle/value changes of one fiat-payment Requirement.

requirements.title: Fiat Buyer Wallet and Reward Access
requirements.definition: A fiat buyer without an existing wallet must receive a low-friction wallet and dashboard path for holding the NFT and accessing commissions and prizes.
requirements.boundary_note: This owns the post-purchase custody and access experience rather than the Transak provider integration itself.

requirements.title: Mint Revenue Distribution
requirements.definition: Each mint payment must be distributed among the founder, affiliate commission, and active prize-pool allocation according to the confirmed business split.
requirements.boundary_note: Revenue allocation is independent of winner selection and the referral recipient-selection rule.

requirements.title: Mint-Page Tipping
requirements.definition: The mint page must offer optional preset or custom tips and clearly communicate any separate follow-up transaction required to send the tip.
requirements.boundary_note: Tip amount selection, transaction UX, and self-tipping safeguards are attributes of one optional tipping mechanism.

requirements.title: Referral Code Identity and Validation
requirements.definition: Each NFT's own mint number must be its permanent referral code, and only already minted eligible NFT numbers may validate as referral codes.
requirements.boundary_note: Code identity and validation are distinct from the monetary and ticket rewards awarded for using a valid code.

requirements.title: Referral Commission
requirements.definition: A successful referred mint must award the configured commission to the NFT or wallet identified by the valid referral code.
requirements.boundary_note: Commission amount and payout belong here; behavior when no code is used belongs to the separate no-referral allocation Requirement.

requirements.title: No-Referral Reward Allocation
requirements.definition: When a mint uses no valid referral code, its commission and applicable prize ticket must be assigned to an existing NFT holder at random, subject to a first-mint exception.
requirements.boundary_note: Random recipient selection is independently changeable from normal code-based commission and ticket issuance.

requirements.title: Prize Ticket Lifecycle
requirements.definition: Qualifying mints must create the applicable prize entries, track them against NFTs, and expire or reset them after their associated draw.
requirements.boundary_note: Ticket issuance and expiration can be tested or changed independently of prize amount, winner count, and claim UX.

requirements.title: Small Block Prize
requirements.definition: The independently evolving small-prize mechanism governs its pool, trigger, winner count, prize amount, eligible entries, and post-draw reset.
requirements.boundary_note: Winner count, prize amount, draw interval, and pool trigger are attributes of one small-prize mechanism.

requirements.title: Big Block Prize
requirements.definition: The historical Big Block mechanism governs its separate high-value prize pool, trigger, entries, winners, and draw reset.
requirements.boundary_note: Big Block changed and was removed independently of the Small Block, so it remains a separate historical Requirement.

requirements.title: Chainlink VRF Randomness
requirements.definition: Random prize winners and random no-referral recipients must use verifiable on-chain randomness through Chainlink VRF.
requirements.boundary_note: The randomness-provider constraint applies across multiple reward mechanisms and can be configured independently of prize values.

requirements.title: Prize Claiming
requirements.definition: Prize winners must have the confirmed payout or claim interaction, including a conditional claim control when a prize is available.
requirements.boundary_note: Claim UX is separable from winner selection and prize-pool funding.

requirements.title: Aave Prize-Pool Yield
requirements.definition: The historical requirement for prize-pool funds to earn yield through an Aave integration.
requirements.boundary_note: Aave yield was independently removable without removing the underlying prize mechanism.

requirements.title: Secondary Sale Rules
requirements.definition: Secondary NFT sales must enforce the configured flat royalty and marketplace controls, contribute as specified to reward pools, and not create referral tickets.
requirements.boundary_note: Royalty enforcement, secondary pool funding, and ticket exclusion are attributes of one secondary-sale mechanism.

requirements.title: NFT Metadata
requirements.definition: Each NFT must expose accurate dynamic metadata and assets, including its own referral code, image, badges, ticket state, and relevant ebook links.
requirements.boundary_note: Metadata representation is distinct from the business rules that produce referral, badge, and ticket values.

requirements.title: NFT-Gated Ebook Access
requirements.definition: Only a valid NFT holder may decrypt and access the ebook through ownership-aware gating, with unauthorized access denied.
requirements.boundary_note: Lit network configuration, wallet signing, and mobile compatibility belong to the access gate rather than PDF rendering.

requirements.title: Ebook Reader
requirements.definition: NFT holders must be able to read the PDF through an integrated read-only viewer with usable page navigation and an optional offline-download path.
requirements.boundary_note: Reader rendering and navigation can fail independently after access control has successfully authorized the holder.

requirements.title: Mint Confirmation Certificate
requirements.definition: A successful buyer with a registered email must be able to receive a mint confirmation or NFT certificate containing identifying details and an ebook-access link.
requirements.boundary_note: Certificate content and availability are separate from general email-delivery infrastructure.

requirements.title: Hybrid Authentication
requirements.definition: The platform must support wallet-based SIWE for crypto actions, email-based low-friction dashboard access, and unauthenticated public APIs.
requirements.boundary_note: Wallet, email, and public access modes are coordinated attributes of one authentication model.

requirements.title: Transactional Email Service
requirements.definition: The platform must use the selected email service to deliver authentication, mint, reward, badge, and account-verification messages reliably.
requirements.boundary_note: Brevo configuration and delivery reliability belong here; the semantic contents of the NFT certificate are separate.

requirements.title: Mint Recording and Supply Accuracy
requirements.definition: Only confirmed successful on-chain mints may be recorded, and displayed total supply, next mint number, and mint status must match the active contract.
requirements.boundary_note: Canonical mint recording is separate from whether owned NFTs render correctly in a user's dashboard.

requirements.title: Owned NFT Dashboard
requirements.definition: The dashboard must show the connected user's actual owned NFTs with usable images, detail pages, and ebook-access controls.
requirements.boundary_note: NFT inventory and asset rendering can fail independently of aggregate reward statistics.

requirements.title: Reward Data Accuracy
requirements.definition: Referral counts, commissions, tickets, prize pools, badge state, and related totals must be consistently accurate across dashboards, leaderboards, public counters, and NFT attributes.
requirements.boundary_note: This owns cross-view state consistency, not the underlying rules that determine who earns each reward.

requirements.title: Mint Success Feedback
requirements.definition: Mint-success feedback must appear only after a real mint and required reward finalization have succeeded, use the correct token ID, and show context-appropriate referral messaging.
requirements.boundary_note: Modal timing and copy are independent from transaction execution and reward accounting.

requirements.title: NFT Achievement Badges
requirements.definition: NFTs and dashboards must provide the approved referral-achievement badges with correct milestones, icons, earned state, notifications, and usable layout.
requirements.boundary_note: Badge definitions and presentation are separate from the general accuracy of commissions and ticket totals.

requirements.title: Mobile Responsive Layout
requirements.definition: Landing-page statistics, mechanics, badges, and other responsive UI elements must stack and remain visible without cutoff on mobile screens.
requirements.boundary_note: Responsive visual layout is separate from mobile-wallet authorization for the ebook reader.

requirements.title: Production Site Availability
requirements.definition: The deployed Project Rebuild web application must remain reachable and usable in production after releases.
requirements.boundary_note: The production outage provides direct evidence of the availability expectation rather than a new product feature.

requirements.title: Discord Community Server
requirements.definition: Project Rebuild must have an operational Discord community with onboarding, announcements, discussion, feedback, support, and bug-report channels.
requirements.boundary_note: Discord setup and channel structure can evolve independently of the website contact form.

requirements.title: End-to-End Production Testing
requirements.definition: The implementation must undergo end-to-end testing of mint paths, referrals, no-referral behavior, prize triggers, metadata, email, ebook access, and payment flows.
requirements.boundary_note: This is the explicit testing obligation; discovered successes and failures also provide execution evidence for their concrete product Requirements.

requirements.title: Contract Migration Continuity
requirements.definition: Contract replacements or upgrades must follow the accepted migration policy for mint numbering, existing NFTs, users, reward state, and retained platform data.
requirements.boundary_note: Migration continuity is a bounded release obligation distinct from the long-term mint and reward rules.

requirements.title: Wallet Trust Warning Resolution
requirements.definition: The project must be submitted for relevant trust-provider verification to remove or prevent the false malicious-site warning shown by wallets or browsers.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a remediation and verification task rather than an application authentication rule.

requirements.title: Client Ownership of Reserved Test Mints
requirements.definition: Specified early production or test NFTs, particularly mint and affiliate code number one, must be transferred to the client's wallet after testing.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a one-off delivery obligation, not a general mint-number assignment rule.

requirements.title: Super Admin Dashboard Specification Document
requirements.definition: Produce the requested task-local document describing the proposed Super Admin dashboard without treating the document request itself as authorization to implement the dashboard.
requirements.boundary_note: Changed by consistency audit.

Hero Headline: Dropout multimillionaire to zero in one oversight. Now rebuilding, with an eBook model to free creators from Amazon's 70% cut.

Sub-Headline: "My Underdog Journey: To Own Goal" — Unlimited NFT book ⋅ $15 forever ⋅ Base.

Mechanics Tease: Buy → own the book + get your referral link. Refer → unlimited, instant $5 + 1 entry to $500 random giveaway, every 100 sales.

Add to mechanics tease: "Refer for instant $5 + your shot at $500 every 100 sales."
This turns it into "ongoing roulette spin" for hustlers.

Add FAQs:
How Does a Non-Crypto Fiat Buyer Collect Commissions and Prizes?
If you're buying with fiat (credit card, Apple Pay, etc.) and new to crypto, don't worry — the process is designed to be simple. When you mint the book for $15 via Transak, a non-custodial wallet is automatically created for you behind the scenes (no seed phrase needed at first). This wallet holds your NFT and receives any commissions or prizes. Here's how it works step by step:

During the Purchase:
Transak handles the fiat-to-crypto conversion and mints the NFT directly to a new wallet address for you. You don't need to set up anything manually — it's seamless and non-custodial (you own the keys, but no complicated seed phrase to manage right away).
You'll get an email confirmation with your mint number (your referral code), NFT details, and a link to your dashboard on <http://projectrebuild.xyz|projectrebuild.xyz>.

Earning Commissions ($5 per Referral):
Share your referral code (e.g., "use 8421"). When someone mints with it, $5 is automatically sent to your wallet address.
To collect: Log into your dashboard on <http://projectrebuild.xyz|projectrebuild.xyz> (using the email link or SIWE with the wallet Transak created). Your commissions appear there instantly — no action needed.

Earning and Winning Prizes:
Each referral gives you a ticket for the current prize draw. These are tied to your NFT/wallet automatically.
Draws happen on-chain ($500, every 100 sales) via fair randomness. Winners are announced on the Winners page and emailed to you.
To collect a prize: If you win, $500 is sent straight to your wallet. Check your dashboard for notifications — we'll email step-by-step instructions to view/claim into fiat if needed (e.g., link to a simple exchange guide). No seed phrase required; use the dashboard to access..

How Do I Collect My Commissions and Prizes? (For Beginners)
If you're new to this, don't worry — everything is automatic and easy to track. Here's how it works step by step:

Earning Commissions ($5 per Referral):
When someone mints the book using your referral code (your mint number, found in your dashboard or email confirmation), $5 is sent straight to your wallet instantly. No action needed from you — the smart contract handles it.

Earning Prize Tickets:
Every successful referral also gives you 1 ticket for the $500 prize, every 100 sales. These are automatically added to your NFT (visible in your dashboard).
No need to do anything — tickets are on-chain and tied to your mint number.

Winning and Collecting Prizes:
Prizes are drawn automatically using Chainlink VRF (a fair random system) when pools hit the trigger (every 100 sales). Winners are announced on the Winners page and via email (if you provided one).
If you win, $500 is sent to your wallet instantly. Check your dashboard for notifications — we'll also email you.
Tickets expire after the draw they're for, but new referrals get you tickets for the next blocks..

Other Wording Tweaks:
Mechanics List: all focus on frequent $500 wins + your $5 commission to reinforce "cut middlemen, funnel savings."

Prize Section: change 'When the prize pool reaches $500 (every 100 sales), 1 winner is randomly selected from all ticket holders using Chainlink VRF for provably fair randomness.' to '**$500 every 100 sales!** 1 affiliate selected (from that 100 sales block), using Chainlink VRF for provably fair randomness. **More referrals = more chances to win!**' — make it the headline for skim.

General: Swap "revolutionary" to "aligned" or "fair" — less hype, more ethos. Add "Help the rebuild — share to earn" tagline below stats.

Visual/UI Tweaks:
Add book cover to hero (integrate with headline).

Live Counters: Add "Next $500 Draw In: ~X Sales" for urgency.
Mobile Test: Ensure stats/mechanics stack well — no cutoff.
